correctness.rationale: All assumptions and quantifiers have been checked. For discrete K, C_0(K) equals c_0(K), with universal NA_2 established in the 2026 primary paper; finite nonempty K are elementary. For any nontrivial convergent sequence, disjoint compact-support cutoffs define norm-one maps E:c->C_0(K) and R:C_0(K)->c with RE=I. A concrete T on c has norm one and no norm-attaining T**: its adjoint is isometrically represented by an ell_1 column operator with columns u/2 and u/2+b_n/2, and its dual cannot attain norm one due to strict positivity of u. The transferred A=ETR is norm one and a norm-attaining A** would give a norm-attaining T**, impossible. First countability gives the converse topology boundary. The exact rational column formula was checked independently on 60 finite indices; the universal conclusion uses the analytic proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: This gives a natural complete topological classification, rather than an arbitrary finite test: for nonempty first-countable locally compact Hausdorff K, fixed-supremum-norm universal second-adjoint attainment on real C_0(K) holds exactly at discreteness. It unifies finite-dimensional positive spaces, infinite discrete c_0(Gamma) positive spaces, and every non-discrete first-countable example (including compact intervals, Cantor-type compacta and their locally compact variants) into one sharp structural boundary. The explicit contractive c-retract explains the obstruction and applies beyond first countability whenever a convergent sequence exists. The precise classification was not a stated consequence in the source and gives a reusable structural obstruction.
